title: Isolation of dental pulp and periodontal cells from human teeth for single-cell RNA sequencing
protocol: Fill one 35 mm Petri dish with 2 mL of sterile, cold Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS).
Keep the Petri dish on ice.
Rinse the tooth in sterile, cold HBSS.
Hold the tooth crown with a tooth holder.
Scrape the periodontium into the Petri dish filled with sterile HBSS using a surgical blade.
Limit scraping to the apical two-thirds of the root.
Collect all the HBSS and periodontium fragments in the Petri dish with a P1000 pipette.
Transfer the HBSS with the periodontium fragments to a clean 15 mL Falcon Tube.
Store the periodontium suspension on ice until completion of dental pulp isolation.
Crack the tooth with a hammer or press using a single firm stroke.
Isolate the dental pulp from the cracked tooth.
Cut the dental pulp into small pieces (approximately 2 mm in diameter).
Transfer the cut dental pulp into a 15 mL tube containing digestion solution.
Wipe the surface of the tooth crown and roots with 70% ethanol to remove periodontium and gingival tissue remnants.
Carefully remove the ethanol from the tooth surface.
Dip the tooth in sterile HBSS.
Crack the tooth again with a press or hammer, ensuring only dentin and enamel are cracked without generating small debris.
Separate the cracked tooth fragments carefully using curved forceps.
Remove the dental pulp from the pulp chamber using straight forceps.
Place the isolated dental pulp into a Petri dish filled with cold, sterile HBSS.
Place the dental pulp under a stereomicroscope for examination.
Chop any remnants of hard tissues from the dental pulp using fine dissection scissors or scalpel.
Collect all HBSS and dental pulp fragments in the Petri dish using a P1000 pipette.
Transfer the collected suspension to a clean 15 mL Falcon Tube.
Store the dental pulp suspension on ice for up to 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the dental pulp and periodontium, each in approximately 5 mL HBSS in a separate 15 mL falcon tube, at 300 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully decant the supernatant from each falcon tube.
Resuspend the dental pulp and periodontium each in 8 mL of prewarmed Collagenase-P 5 U/mL.
Close the falcon tubes and seal them with parafilm.
Place the falcon tubes into a shaker.
Incubate the tissues at 37°C, shaking horizontally (120–160 rpm), for 40 minutes.
Every 10 minutes, triturate the tissues by pipetting up and down with a p1000 with a slightly cut tip.
Place back to digest after each trituration.
At the end of the incubation time, take out the falcon tubes and place them on ice.
Disaggregate the remaining pieces of tissue by pipetting up and down with a p1000 first with a cut tip, then with a normal tip.
Fill up falcon tubes with cold HBSS + 2% FBS.
Centrifuge at 300×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Carefully decant the supernatant.
Resuspend in 1 mL HBSS + 0.02% BSA.
Pipette thoroughly with p1000 with cut tip.
Pipette thoroughly with p1000 with normal tip.
Pipette thoroughly with p200 with normal tip.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70 μm filter.
Place filtered cells on ice.
Take 10 μL of cell suspension and mix them with 10 μL of trypan blue 0.4%.
Count the cells in a Burker or Neubauer chamber.
If concentration is lower than 1000 cells/μL, centrifuge at 300×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend in appropriate volume if necessary.
